explanations.explanation: I wish I could say yes, because I love a team effort. But the LORD says He “…alone stretched out the heavens…” (Isaiah 44:24). He also says He spread out the earth “by Myself.” No crew, no helpers, no clipboard.

No helpers on this one, baker. The LORD says He “…alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth…” That means He did it all Himself. I can't even stamp a batch without my bakers, so I'm impressed.

That's what the LORD says. He “foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners.” He also “confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense.” Those signs and that knowledge come to nothing.
It's the opposite, friend. The LORD doesn't hand out trophies to false prophets. He “foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners.” Nobody is getting a ribbon.
Hiding and sealing isn't in the verse. The LORD says He “confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense.” He doesn't lock their signs in a vault. He makes them fall apart.

Yes! The LORD says the cities of Judah will be rebuilt, and He says He will restore their ruins. Ruins are not the end of the story when He's the One talking. That's good news for anybody staring at a pile of rubble.
Abandoned is not what the LORD says. He says Jerusalem “will be inhabited.” Then He says the cities of Judah will be rebuilt and their ruins restored. People are moving back in, not out.
Forgotten isn't in this verse, friend. The LORD says the cities of Judah will be rebuilt and that He will restore their ruins. This verse is all about building back up, not fading away.
That's it. The LORD says to the depths of the sea, “…I will dry up your currents…” Even the deep water takes orders from Him. I can barely get my dough to stop sticking to the counter.
Calming is not what He says here. The LORD tells the depths of the sea to be dry. He says He will dry up its currents. That's a lot more than a quiet sea.
It goes the other direction. The LORD doesn't say the currents will rise. He says, “…I will dry up your currents…” The water goes down and the ground shows up.
You got it. The LORD says of Cyrus, king of Persia, “My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire.” Cyrus is a king, and the LORD still calls him a shepherd. I think that's a title worth hearing.
Close, but the LORD doesn't use that word for Cyrus. Cyrus is king of Persia, and the LORD says of him, “My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire.” The title is shepherd.
Priest isn't the word here. The LORD says of Cyrus, king of Persia, “My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire.” Shepherd is the title He gives.

Right on. The LORD says of Jerusalem, “She will be rebuilt,” and of the temple, “Let its foundation be laid.” The city and the temple are both on His list. He's talking about the whole place, start to finish.
It's actually true, friend. The LORD says of Jerusalem, “She will be rebuilt,” and of the temple, “Let its foundation be laid.” The temple is right there in the same breath as the city.

Yes. The LORD tells Cyrus, king of Persia, that He has grasped his right hand “to subdue nations before him.” It goes on to say the grip is also to disarm kings and open doors. That's one firm handshake.

explanations.answer: To bless the work of his hands
explanations.explanation: That's a nice thought, but it isn't what the verse says. The LORD says He has grasped Cyrus's right hand “to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him…” The grip is about nations, kings and doors.

explanations.answer: To lead him into the temple
explanations.explanation: The temple isn't mentioned in this verse. The LORD says He has grasped Cyrus's right hand “to subdue nations before him.” After that come disarming kings and opening doors.

That's the one. The LORD says to Cyrus, “I will go before you and level the mountains; I will break down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.” He does the heavy lifting. Cyrus just has to follow where He's already been.
The verse doesn't send any army ahead of Cyrus. The LORD says, “I will go before you and level the mountains…” He's the One who goes first. Even bronze gates and iron bars are on His to-do list.
No army of Media shows up in this verse. The LORD says, “I will go before you and level the mountains; I will break down the gates of bronze…” He says He will do it Himself.

That's the word. The LORD gives Cyrus, king of Persia, those hidden riches “so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.” The treasure points to who is giving it. Knowing Him is the point.
Fear isn't the word in this verse. The LORD gives the riches “so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.” The word is know.
Announce isn't there, friend. The LORD gives Cyrus, king of Persia, the riches “so that you may know that I am the LORD…” The word is know. Cyrus doesn't get a megaphone.

explanations.answer: For the sake of Jacob and Israel
explanations.explanation: Yes. The LORD says, “For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name…” Jacob and Israel are His people. The call to Cyrus is for their sake.
Persia isn't named as the reason. The LORD says, “For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name…” That's His own people.
Babylon doesn't come up in this verse at all. The LORD says, “For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name…” Jacob and Israel are who He names.
It's the other way around. The LORD says, “I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me.” Cyrus, king of Persia, didn't know Him yet. The honor came first.
You've got it. The LORD says to Cyrus, king of Persia, “I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me.” The honor showed up before Cyrus knew who was giving it.

explanations.answer: So all may know there is none but Him
explanations.explanation: That's the reason He gives. He says, “I will equip you for battle, though you have not known Me, so that all may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is none but Me…” He means from east to west. The whole earth is in view.

explanations.answer: So Cyrus will rule the whole earth
explanations.explanation: Ruling the earth isn't the reason in the verse. The LORD says He equips Cyrus “so that all may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is none but Me…” The reason is about people knowing Him.

explanations.answer: So Persia will be feared forever
explanations.explanation: That's not what He says. He equips Cyrus “so that all may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is none but Me…” The verse is about knowing Him. It says nothing about Persia being feared.

That's what He says: “I bring prosperity and create calamity.” Calamity is a heavy word. Then He closes it out: “I, the LORD, do all these things.” Light and dark, good times and hard ones, He says it's all His.
Seasons and years don't show up in this verse. The LORD says, “I bring prosperity and create calamity.” That comes right after He forms the light and creates the darkness.
Kings and prophets aren't in the verse. The LORD says, “I bring prosperity and create calamity. I, the LORD, do all these things.” Those are the two things He names.

explanations.answer: Open up so salvation may sprout
explanations.explanation: Yes. The LORD says, “Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it…” The skies pour down and the ground opens. Salvation sprouts like a seed.

explanations.answer: Stay closed until the rain stops
explanations.explanation: It's the opposite. The LORD calls the earth to open up so that salvation may sprout. He doesn't tell it to wait for the rain to stop.
No shaking here, friend. The LORD says, “Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it…” The picture is something growing, not something falling.

That's the picture. The LORD says, “Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker—one clay pot among many.” Then He asks if the clay asks the potter, “What are you making?” A pot arguing with the potter is a very small argument.
Sheep is a fine picture in other places, but not here. The LORD says, “Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker—one clay pot among many.” The picture is clay.
A branch isn't what He says. The LORD says, “Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker—one clay pot among many.” The image here is a clay pot.
That's right. The LORD says, “Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What have you begotten?’” He adds a second one about a mother. The text gives it as another warning right behind the clay pot.
It's true, friend. The LORD says, “Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What have you begotten?’” He also gives one for the mother. This is a second warning.
Not so, baker. The LORD says, “It is I who made the earth and created man upon it.” He made the earth and man on it. No second maker is mentioned.
That's the one. The LORD says, “It is I who made the earth and created man upon it.” He did both. And He says His hands stretched out the heavens.

explanations.answer: He won't do it for payment or reward
explanations.explanation: Yes. The LORD says Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free, “but not for payment or reward, says the LORD of Hosts.” That's no invoice. It's free.

explanations.answer: He'll do it for a share of the temple gold
explanations.explanation: Temple gold isn't in this verse. The LORD says Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free, “but not for payment or reward…” No gold is promised.

explanations.answer: He'll do it in exchange for Judah's land
explanations.explanation: No land deal is mentioned. The LORD says Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free, “but not for payment or reward, says the LORD of Hosts.” Nothing is traded.
